title: BenGER: Benchmarking LLM Systems on Subsumption-Based Legal Reasoning in German Law
abstract: arXiv:2605.28183v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We introduce BenGER (Benchmark for German Law), a benchmark and dataset for evaluating LLM systems on subsumption-based legal reasoning in German law. The dataset combines 596 exam-style free-text legal case tasks across multiple levels of legal education and 531 short doctrinal reasoning tasks. It includes a controlled validation subset of timed human-written solutions under both unaided and human-AI co-creation conditions. We evaluate 12 contemporary LLM systems - closed flagship, efficiency-oriented, and open-weight - with a rubric-aligned LLM-as-a-Judge cross-validated against a multi-rater human-grading layer (three blind reviews per solution, six judge families benchmarked against the human pool). Closed-flagship systems lead the leaderboard across all three corpora, human-AI co-creation measurably improves on unaided human work, and the LLM judge tracks human grading at Pearson r=0.76 and Cohen's k=0.60. translated_title: BenGER：基于涵摄式法律推理的德国法LLM系统基准测试
translated_abstract: 我们提出BenGER（德国法基准），这是一个用于评估LLM系统在德国法涵摄式法律推理能力的基准和数据集。该数据集包含596个覆盖多个法学教育层次的考试风格自由文本法律案例任务，以及531个简短的法理推理任务。数据集还包括一个受控验证子集，收集了在无辅助和人机协同创作两种条件下限时完成的人类书面解答。我们评估了12个当代LLM系统——包括闭源旗舰模型、效率导向模型和开源权重模型——采用与评分细则对齐的LLM-as-a-Judge方法，并与多评分者人工评分层进行交叉验证（每份解答经过三次盲评，六个评审模型系列与人类评分池进行基准对比）。结果显示：闭源旗舰系统在所有三个语料库中均位居排行榜首位，人机协同创作相较无辅助的人类工作有可测量的提升，且LLM评审与人类评分高度一致（Pearson r=0.76，Cohen's k=0.60）。
tldr: 该论文提出BenGER基准，通过596个考试风格案例任务和531个法理推理任务评估12个LLM系统在德国法涵摄式推理上的能力，发现闭源旗舰模型表现领先、人机协同创作优于纯人类解答，且LLM评审与人类评分高度一致。
en_tdlr: BenGER is a benchmark and dataset for evaluating 12 contemporary LLM systems on subsumption-based legal reasoning in German law, finding that closed flagship systems lead the leaderboard, human-AI co-creation measurably improves on unaided human work, and the LLM-as-a-Judge approach closely tracks human grading (Pearson r=0.76, Cohen's k=0.60).
